ai.literal: Without embracing, stay; you sulk! He will experience distress pain, let us see a little.
ai.translation: Stay without embracing him and keep sulking! Let us watch for a little while the painful distress he suffers.
ai.modern: அவரைத் தழுவாமல் விலகி இரு; நீ ஊடல் கொள்! அதனால் அவர் அடையும் துன்ப நோயை நாம் சிறிது நேரம் வேடிக்கை பார்ப்போம்.
ai.explanation: The heroine's friend advises her to prolong her feigned anger. She tells the heroine to stay away without embracing her lover and to keep sulking. The friend playfully suggests that they should watch the sweet distress and pain he experiences when he is denied her affection. The word 'காண்கம்' (let us see) highlights the playful, shared conspiracy between the women.

ai.literal: Sulking is like salt being sufficient; letting that prolong is like exceeding a little.
ai.translation: A lover's sulking is like adding just enough salt to food. Prolonging it is like adding a little too much.
ai.modern: உணவில் உப்பு சரியான அளவில் இருப்பது போல காதலில் ஊடல் இருப்பது சுவை தரும். அந்த ஊடலை அளவுக்கு மீறி நீட்டிக்கச் செய்வது, உணவில் உப்பு சிறிது அதிகமாகிவிட்டதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a lover's feigned anger to salt in food. Just as the right amount of salt enhances the taste of a dish, a brief period of sulking adds charm to love. However, if the sulking is prolonged, it ruins the joy of the relationship, exactly as adding even a little too much salt makes food inedible. The words 'amaintu' (being optimal) and 'mikku' (exceeding) perfectly capture this delicate balance.

ai.literal: To those who are distressed, sorrow and pain having caused, it is like, oneself, those who sulked, without embracing, leaving.
ai.translation: Leaving without embracing those who sulk with you is like inflicting further sorrow and pain on those who are already distressed.
ai.modern: தம்மிடம் ஊடல் கொண்டவரைத் தழுவி சமாதானம் செய்யாமல் அப்படியே விட்டுவிடுவது, ஏற்கனவே துன்பப்படுபவர்களுக்கு மேலும் துன்பத்தையும் வலியையும் தருவதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet illustrates the emotional cruelty of ignoring a lover's affectionate sulking. The word 'புலந்தார்' denotes a partner who feigns anger, expecting to be pacified. Leaving them without an embrace ('புல்லா விடல்') intensifies their longing and hurt. The poet compares this neglect to inflicting additional sorrow and pain ('அல்லல் நோய்') on someone who is already in deep distress ('அலந்தார்'). This vivid analogy emphasizes that a sulking lover is vulnerable and needs immediate comfort, not abandonment.

ai.literal: Those who sulked not appeasing, withered creeper's root having cut is like.
ai.translation: Failing to appease a sulking partner is like cutting a withered creeper at its root.
ai.modern: ஊடல் கொண்டவரைச் சமாதானம் செய்யாமல் இருப்பது, ஏற்கனவே வாடிப்போன கொடியை அதன் வேரிலேயே அறுப்பதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares a lover's sulking to a withered creeper. When a creeper is already wilting, it needs water and care to revive, not further harm. Similarly, when a partner is sulking, they are emotionally fragile and need to be comforted. Ignoring their feelings and failing to appease them is as destructive as cutting the root of a dying plant, which will kill the relationship completely.

ai.literal: Deep sulking and feigned anger if absent, love is like ripe fruit and unripe fruit.
ai.translation: In love, deep sulking is like a bitter unripe fruit, and the complete absence of playful sulking is like a cloying overripe fruit.
ai.modern: காதலில் நீண்ட ஊடல் இருந்தால் அது முதிராத கருக்காயைப் போன்றது; செல்லமான சிறு ஊடலும் இல்லாவிட்டால் அது மிகவும் கனிந்த பழத்தைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a poetic cross-mapping to contrast two extremes in lovers' quarrels. 'துனி' (deep, prolonged anger) makes love harsh and bitter, like an unripe fruit ('கருக்காய்'). Conversely, if 'புலவி' (light, playful sulking) is completely absent ('இல்லாயின்'), love becomes too sweet and soft, like an overripe fruit ('கனி'). The poet suggests that ideal love requires just the right amount of playful friction to be perfectly enjoyable, neither too hard nor too soft.

ai.literal: In feigned anger there is there a sorrow, 'uniting prolonging is it not [doubt]?' thinking.
ai.translation: Even in a lovers' quarrel there is a certain sorrow, born of the anxious thought that their coming together might be delayed.
ai.modern: ஊடலிலும், மீண்டும் ஒன்று சேருவது தாமதமாகுமோ என்று எண்ணுவதால் ஒரு துன்பம் இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the delicate psychological state of a lover during a feigned quarrel (ஊடல்). Although such a quarrel is meant to eventually enhance the pleasure of union, it brings its own subtle sorrow (துன்பம்). This pain arises from the anxious thought (என்று) that the time taken to finally reunite (புணர்வது) might be prolonged (நீடுவது). The particles of doubt (அன்று கொல்) perfectly express the lover's hesitation and fear of an extended separation.

ai.explanation: This couplet questions the value of feigning anger or sulking when the lover is not perceptive enough to notice it. The word 'நோதல்' refers to the mental distress or the act of sulking in a romantic quarrel. It highlights that the pleasure of a lover's quarrel depends entirely on the partner's attentive and soothing response.

ai.literal: Water-even of the shade sweet-indeed; sulking-also lovers with-indeed sweet.
ai.translation: Even water is pleasant only when it is in the shade. Sulking is pleasant only with those who love.
ai.modern: நீரும் நிழலில் இருக்கும்போதே இனிமையாக இருக்கும். அதுபோல, ஊடலும் அன்புடையவர்களிடம் கொள்ளும்போதே இனிமையாக இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: Water gives true refreshment only when it is kept cool in the shade. In the same way, feigned anger or sulking is enjoyable only when it happens between true lovers. If there is no underlying love, sulking will only cause bitterness rather than sweet reconciliation. The couplet uses the natural image of shaded water to show how the context of deep affection makes temporary disagreements pleasant.

ai.literal: Sulking to wither with him who lets, my heart 'we will join' saying that is desire.
ai.translation: It is pure desire that makes my heart say, 'We will unite with him who lets my sulking wither away.'
ai.modern: என் ஊடல் வாடிப் போகும்படி என்னை விட்டுவிடுகின்ற அவரோடு, 'நாம் ஒன்று சேருவோம்' என்று என் நெஞ்சம் நினைப்பது அதன் ஆசையினால்தான்.
ai.explanation: The speaker is upset that her lover does not try to pacify her feigned anger, but instead leaves her to suffer and let the anger wither away on its own. Despite his indifference, her heart still yearns to be united with him. She realizes that her heart's readiness to yield and say 'we will join him' is driven entirely by its overwhelming desire for him, overriding her pride. The word 'uṇaṅka' vividly captures the painful withering of her unresolved sulking.
